pages.chapter: PART I — PRESENTATION AND HISTORY OF THE HURON-WENDAT NATION
claimsCompared: the Nation’s own description of its territory: “the customary territory of the Huron-Wendat Nation, the Nionwentsïo, which means “our magnificent land” in the Huron-Wendat language, lies along the north and south shores of the St. Lawrence River, between the Saint-Maurice River and the Saguenay River”
the St. Lawrence as “the Great River according to the Huron-Wendat oral tradition, which is situated at the very core of the Nionwentsïo”
the point-in-time membership figure: "The Huron-Wendat Nation has approximately 4,000 members"
"Almost all of the Huron-Wendat members reside in Wendake, the only Huron-Wendat reserve in Canada."
the treaty basis: "The Huron-British Treaty of 1760", and the Sioui ruling's "over the entire territory frequented by the Hurons"
the filing: submitted to the Standing Committee on Transport, Infrastructure and Communities from Wendake, Quebec, dated December 7, 2016
